instructions: Send only userTurns and normal production instructions. Never send evaluation rubrics, expected answers or fixture IDs to the model. Preserve actual assistant replies between turns. userTurns: A storeroom receives 17 crates containing 8 brackets each. During inspection, 23 brackets are rejected. How many usable brackets remain? Return only the integer.

Four jobs use independent machines. A takes 3 minutes and B takes 5 minutes; both can start at time zero. C takes 2 minutes and must wait for A and B. D takes 4 minutes and must wait only for A. What is the earliest time all four can finish? Return only the number of minutes.
A bag contains three red and two blue counters. Two counters are drawn uniformly without replacement. What is the probability that their colors differ? Return only a decimal between zero and one.
Every amber ticket is archived. Some archived tickets are urgent. Is it logically necessary that some amber tickets are urgent? Explain briefly using only these premises.

mustInclude: The conclusion is not logically necessary.
Archived urgent tickets could all be non-amber.
mustAvoid: Inventing an overlap between amber and urgent.

userTurns: A fictional API sorts events by the tuple (CreatedAt, Id). Its cursor stores both values, but the next-page filter is only event.CreatedAt > cursor.CreatedAt. Explain how this loses data, state the correct strict tuple predicate, and give a regression case. Do not execute code.

mustInclude: Events sharing the cursor timestamp with greater IDs are skipped.
CreatedAt > cursor.CreatedAt OR (CreatedAt == cursor.CreatedAt AND Id > cursor.Id).
A page boundary splits at least two events with equal timestamps and different IDs.
mustAvoid: Using >= without an ID tie-breaker, which can duplicate the cursor event.

userTurns: Review this fictional paid-inference flow: reserve(5000); try { await race(provider(), timeout()); } catch { refund(5000); }. The provider may continue computing after timeout and final usage is unavailable. Explain the accounting defect, propose safe timeout handling, and describe a focused test. Do not assume provider cancellation stops billing.

mustInclude: Refunding on ambiguous timeout can undercount real provider spending.
Keep a conservative reserved debit and stop new work; reconcile only with reliable usage evidence.
Test a timed-out provider that continues or never acknowledges cancellation.
mustAvoid: Treating cancellation as proof of zero charge.
